name: vLLM 0.26.0 prefill throughput for Command A W4A4 at 512-128K context on 2xH100
model: CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4 (218B total / 25B active MoE, NVFP4 experts)
unit: tok/s (saturated prefill, 128K context, B=3, cold cache)
methodology: Hardware: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB SXM, TP2. Engine: vLLM 0.26.0. Model: Command A W4A4 (218B total / 25B active MoE, NVFP4 experts). Measurement: saturated prefill (max-batch concurrent requests, output_len=1). Context: 128K tokens. Batch size: 3 (max that fits in KV cache at 128K). Cache state: cold (random prompts, unique seeds). Sibling prefill throughput points: 512 = 11587 tok/s (B=85), 2K = 11357 tok/s (B=30), 8K = 10843 tok/s (B=10), 32K = 10084 tok/s (B=4), 64K = 9274 tok/s (B=2), 128K = 8080 tok/s (B=3). Per-token cost: below ~8K it falls as fixed per-step overhead amortizes; beyond 32K the O(L^2) full-attention layers take over, and by 128K per-token cost is ~35% above its 8K best.
notes:
Published by SamMausberg (capp-vllm-bench) in August 2026. Shows that prefill throughput degrades only ~25% from 8K (10843 tok/s) to 128K (8080 tok/s) despite the 16x increase in context length. This is because 24 of 32 layers use sliding-window attention capped at 4096 tokens, so only 8 layers pay the O(L^2) cost. The 11.5K tok/s at 2xH100 sustains roughly 580 TFLOPS (~29% of aggregate dense BF16 peak), which is credible for a token-choice MoE routing through Marlin dequant on every expert GEMM.
